title: How IEDs Work
summary: Josh and Chuck explain improvised explosive devices (IEDs): what they are, their history from Vietnam and the IRA to Iraq and Afghanistan, the five basic components (power supply, trigger, detonator, main charge, container), how blasts injure people, and countermeasures such as jammers, lasers, armored and V-shaped vehicles, dogs, and the fraudulent ADE 651 bomb detector. The episode also includes a listener email about a hyperbaric chamber and divers in Utila, Honduras.

entities.name: Joint Improvised Explosive Device Defeat Organization

segments.title: Opening banter and Michael Stipe shirts
segments.summary: Hosts joke about Josh's Mystery Science Theater shirt, fan shirts, and a Michael Stipe sculpture, then introduce the topic of IEDs.

segments.title: IEDs in Iraq and Afghanistan: history and definition
segments.summary: Chuck defines the improvised explosive device and the hosts discuss IED casualties in Iraq and Afghanistan, the shift from gunfire to IEDs, and early armored vehicle shortages. They trace IEDs to Vietnam (Viet Cong cans on roadsides) and the IRA, and note that homemade bombs differ from commercial ones.

segments.title: Why IEDs are used and online bomb-making information
segments.summary: The hosts discuss why insurgents favor IEDs: they are cheap, easy to assemble, and effective against conventional armies. They cite the Times Square attempt and Boston bombing as examples of bomb designs that circulate online.

segments.title: Public event security and bag restrictions
segments.summary: The hosts discuss fear at public events after the Boston bombing, NFL stadium bag restrictions, and tradeoffs between security and stress or racial profiling.

segments.title: Five basic parts of an IED
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck list the components of an IED: power supply, trigger, detonator, main charge, and container, with shrapnel and other fillers. The hosts stay general and avoid step-by-step construction details.

segments.title: How IED triggers and charges fit together and supply chains
segments.summary: The hosts describe how the trigger, detonator, and main charge connect, including timer, trip wire, and remote cell phone triggers, and the Chechen Red Square anecdote. They note that components are easy to obtain, making supply lines hard to trace, and discuss the Pentagon's JIEDDO effort and Pakistan's fertilizer exports.

segments.title: Blast physics and injuries
segments.summary: The hosts describe the blast wave speed, pressure up to a thousand atmospheres, secondary shrapnel, vacuum effect, traumatic brain injury, and perforated lungs and bowels. They note rising limb loss and brain injuries among wounded soldiers in Afghanistan.

segments.title: Countermeasures: detection, jamming, armored vehicles, and fraud
segments.summary: The hosts cover countermeasures: dogs, vigilance, NERF jammers, LIBS laser detection, microwave devices, and armored MRAP vehicles with V-shaped hulls. They discuss James McCormick, who sold the fake ADE 651 detector, and Oshkosh's unmanned Terra Max vehicle.

segments.title: Wrap-up and listener mail
segments.summary: Hosts point listeners to the suicide bombers episode and the search bar, then begin listener mail.

segments.title: Listener mail: hyperbaric chamber in Utila
segments.summary: James writes about working with a hyperbaric chamber on Utila, Honduras, describing dangerous lobster diving conditions and a diver he flew to the mainland. Hosts sign off with contact info.
